purpose: distribute traffic across healthy instances with the right algorithm, health checks and failure behavior, and prove it by testing
entry_criteria: The service has more than one instance or zone
procedure: Choose layer 4 or layer 7 based on needs for routing, TLS handling and headers, and the algorithm based on request cost, such as least connections for uneven requests.
Define health checks that test real readiness (dependencies reachable), with thresholds that neither flap nor hide failures.
Handle state: keep instances stateless, or use session affinity only where required and state the failure effect.
Spread instances across zones, and check that losing one zone leaves enough capacity.
Configure connection draining, timeouts, retry rules that are safe for idempotent requests, and rate limits.
Test by removing an instance and a zone under load, and verify traffic shifts without errors beyond the agreed budget.
acceptance_criteria: Health checks test readiness, not only that the process runs
Capacity covers the loss of one zone
Failure tests were run under load
validation_method: Network engineer and service owner review.

validation.command: for i in $(seq 1 200); do curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' https://app.example.com/; done | sort | uniq -c   # run while one instance is stopped
validation.expect: no more than the agreed share of non-200 responses

validation.check: compute total capacity minus one zone against peak load
validation.expect: remaining capacity is at least peak

worked_example: ILLUSTRATIVE: Three instances across three zones use least-connections balancing with a readiness endpoint that checks the database; stopping one instance under load causes two failed requests out of 2,000 before it leaves rotation, and draining prevents cut-off requests on deploy.
